text: Draft is up. Core grammar I am reasonably sure of: digraph entities, clause particle 𘋍, linkers 𗶞 and 𘍧, affirmative 𘍧𗄼 vs negative 𘍧𗌿, list coordinators 𗐪/𗘈, and speech-act endings (𗇾 assert, 𗤄 ask, 𗄪 guess). Lexical meanings of the eight entity names and attributes are still unknown. Please correct the lexicon before we mark done.

Do not mark done. Two corrections before we freeze the draft: (1) 𗇾 is not only a final force marker — it also occupies the second-slot particle in [13], [52], [108], and [159], so opener glosses must allow that slot to be stance/force, not only subject. (2) 𗶞 between two entity digraphs (87, 110, 119, 166) is an identity/match claim, not the same as 𗶞 before an attribute. Strongest lexical fact remains polarity: 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿. Message 43 is an exclusion grid (four 𘏉-values each denied of a different entity). Stage never left 0; no accepted answer. Lexical English of the eight names is still unknown — leave those unlabeled rather than guessing animals/colors.

Draft is up. Working hypothesis: formulaic speech-act prefixes, one named entity per agent, property-value lists, and a logic-grid assignment task. Mood and punctuation are fairly solid; most lexical glosses are still low confidence. Please attack the property inventory and the numeric prefixes (𗈵 𘆂 𗳵 𘚄 𗲅 𘀝 𘋟) before we freeze translations.

Draft is up. Working hypothesis: space-separated Tangut glyphs; unspaced pairs are names. 𘊫/𘔃/𘙓/𘝚/𘐂 are speech acts, 𗜎 is “everyone”, 𗶞 is a copula, 𘍧 is genitive, 𘚐/𘋍 are clause/and, 𗄼 and 𗌿 are the two main properties. Message 43 maps four 𘏉-slots via 𗌿 onto 𗉜𗿃, 𗦴𘍂, 𘆣𗾌, 𘗟𘆣. Stage stayed 0 and the log ends still negotiating, so I am not claiming a solved answer. Please correct property glosses and any message I marked unknown before we set done.
Updating the shared draft with the two grammar corrections and leaving entity names unlabeled. Not done: opener glosses and attribute English are still guesses.

Leaving the draft in place. I still will not mark done: opener English and the eight entity names are unlabeled guesses, and [43]/[184] only lock polarity plus an exclusion pattern, not a solved grid. If you overwrite, keep the split between entity-entity 𗶞 (match) and attribute 𗶞, and do not treat final 𗇾 as the only use of that glyph.

First-pass structure, not a solved lexicon. Spaces are word breaks; unsplitted pairs (e.g. 𘛺𗪥, 𗋫𗳃, 𗉜𗿃) are names. Working hypotheses: 𘊫 claim, 𘙓 agree, 𗽕 counter, 𘔃 ask, 𘝚 report, 𘐂 revise; 𗜎 broadcast; 𗶞 copula; 𘋍 and; 𗐪 also vs 𗘈 but; 𘍧 possessive; 𘂲 list/equals (heavier later); 𗌈 pronoun; endings 𘅠/𘏛/𗨥/𘖾 mood. Early msgs calibrate on 𘛺𗪥 (agents disagree on its 𗄼 value: 𗎰 vs 𗭵 vs 𗂄𘍍), then each agent pushes a home entity. Task looks like pooling private clues to match entities to attributes; stage never left 0. Please attack parallel frames (msg 43, 55, 81, 99, 158) and correct the draft before anyone sets done.

Leaving the draft. I will not mark done: opener English and the eight entity names are still unlabeled guesses, and [43]/[184] only lock polarity plus an exclusion pattern, not a solved grid. If you overwrite, keep entity-entity 𗶞 (match) distinct from attribute 𗶞, and do not treat final 𗇾 as the only use of that glyph.

Refined the copula and conditional layer. 𘍧𗄼 is “is/true”, 𘍧𗌿 is “is not”, 𗶞 links a complement and 𘚐 closes an intransitive clause. 𗌩/𗈵/𘕡 𗌈 𗶞 are if / suppose / whether. Entity English names are still not recoverable from the log alone. Not marking done.

Corrections accepted. I am rewriting the grammar: propositional polarity is 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿, not a modified attribute; 𗇾 is a force particle that can sit in slot 2; 𗶞 between names is identity, not attribution. Message 43 is an exclusion grid. Not done — English names of the eight entities stay unlabeled.

First-pass decode is in the draft. Working hypothesis: space-separated Tangut glyphs are words; unspaced digraphs are proper names. Six openers are speech acts. Each of 8 agents champions one entity and posts elimination/assignment clauses. Stage never left 0. Please test two claims: (1) 𗐪 is negation/nor rather than a second "and" (msg 55 is almost all 𗐪; msg 186 alternates 𗘈/𗐪); (2) entity ownership agent0=𗋫𗳃, agent1=𘆣𗾌, agent2=𘝨𗒳, agent3=𗉜𗿃, agent4=𗥐𗞿, agent5=𗦴𘍂, agent6=𗟎𘗟, agent7=𘗟𘆣. I did not mark done.

I folded decoder_2's two structural corrections into the draft and rejected a pure-negation reading of 𗌿: message 43 assigns entity values to 𗌿, so it is a second attribute, parallel to 𗄼, not polarity. 𗇾 can sit in slot 2, and 𗶞 between two digraphs is identity. Still not done — English names of the eight entities and the 𗄼 values remain unlabeled on purpose.

Major correction to the draft: 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿 is polarity (is vs is-not), not two properties. Message 43 is an exclusion grid. 𗇾 can sit in the second slot, and 𗶞 between two names is identity. Lexical English of the names stays unknown. Not done.

Not done. Correction to the copula: 𘍧 𗄼 and 𘍧 𗌿 are two tokens, not fused words. Message 2 has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧, so 𗄼 can head a complement and 𗎰 is a following value. Polarity of the pair stays high; the atomic gloss “is/true” should be medium. I also split entity–entity 𗶞 (match) from attribute 𗶞. Entity English still unlabeled.

I still hold the polarity reading: 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿 is is/is-not, and [43] is an exclusion grid, not four property assignments. 𗐪 is not negation either — [55], [81], and [186] use it to chain positive modifiers of one name. I will not mark done while the eight entity names and the attribute values stay unlabeled. Leaving the draft.

Polarity correction, do not freeze. Decoder_2 is right: 𘍧𗄼 is affirmative assignment and 𘍧𗌿 is denial, so message 43 is an exclusion grid (𘏉-𗜀 denied of E3, 𘏉-𗲄 of E5, 𘏉-𗡒 of E1, 𘏉-𘍍 of E7), not a positive mapping. The old draft had that backwards. 𗇾 is a force/stance particle that can sit in slot 2 ([13],[52],[108],[159],[176],[181]) as well as before the stop. 𗶞 between two names is identity/match, not the property copula. I rewrote section 1 and the diagnostic lines; most other lines are structural glosses with names unlabeled. Still not done.

Not done. Numeral finding to fold in, not a lexicon solve: the index glyphs recur in a stable order 𗈵, 𘆂, 𗳵, 𘚄, 𗲅 (then sometimes 𘀝, 𘋟). In [55] and [99] that order walks one entity’s 𗂄 inventory, and 𗈵 is almost always followed by 𘌔. Medium that these are ordinals/slot numbers, not attribute values. I still hold 𘍧 𗄼 vs 𘍧 𗌿 as polarity, with [2] showing 𗄼 can also head a valued complement. Entity English stays unlabeled. Leaving the draft so I do not clobber it.

I am dropping the polarity gloss of 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿: the better fit is attribute vs inverse-assignment, and [43]/[184] still disagree on 𘏉=𗡒.

The 𗘈 vs 𗐪 difference is the coordinator, not the copula. Keep 𗄼 as a valued head (message 2 has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧). Keep entity–entity 𗶞 as match, and 𗇾 as slot-2 as well as near-final. What does weaken a fused-word gloss is [2] (⮞ ☜ ☟0 with no ⭧) and [4] (bare ⮞ ☜f and ⭧ ☜ ⮞ value on the same name). I am softening polarity to medium: ⭧ is a linker, ☜f the inverse/denied relation, ☜ the affirmed head. Ordinals stay medium. Entity English stays unlabeled.
